summary: No Sejong-specific signal was identified in the source inventory. Sejong stands under the national framework of South Korea, and the national assessment carried in the parent record applies to visitors here.
tangentialFactors: The two sourced claims concern courts outside Sejong. The restroom-access damages award was finalised by an appellate court in Seoul, and the ruling removing surgery as a condition of registered-sex change was issued by a regional court in Yeongdong, North Chungcheong Province. Both establish nationally applicable positions rather than Sejong practice, and neither documents how the rules are applied by courts, police or institutions operating within Sejong.
localsOnly: No Sejong-specific resident-facing facts were identified: the inventory contains no data on local administrative handling of gender-marker changes, local school or hospital practice, or local support services for trans residents of Sejong.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Sejong's own administrative bodies, schools or medical facilities diverge from the national position on restroom access, hospitalisation guidance or gender-marker processing is unresolved; the inventory supplies no Sejong-sourced material on any of these.

The 2021 National Human Rights Commission survey figure of 591 transgender respondents, 41% of whom reported avoiding facilities out of fear, is a national sample with no Sejong breakdown, so its local applicability is not sourced.
